title: Marsa Boulevard
intro:
Marsa Boulevard is back on Dubai Creek for the 2026/27 season, and this year's line-up is its biggest yet. The open-air waterfront strip in Marsa Al Khor, right next to Dubai Festival City Mall, now has 23 restaurants, cafés and dessert spots lined up along the water – and it's only around 10 minutes' drive from Downtown Dubai.

This guide covers every spot open on Marsa Boulevard right now. For each one you'll see what they serve and their latest Instagram post, so you can get a feel for the food and the setting before you go. Where a spot has shared its Marsa Boulevard menu, tap "Marsa Menu" to see exactly what's on offer at this location (not a menu from another branch) – handy for checking prices and planning who's having what.

For coffee, there's Ethr, For a While, Lune, Nuwa, Orto and TRIO. For a proper sit-down meal, try NAC's French bistro, Somewhere's Middle Eastern fusion, contemporary Japanese at Nama Yoso, ramen and handrolls at SLRP, Emirati bistro Murmur, Mediterranean fusion at Mara, Levantine at Three by Eva or izakaya-style Japanese at Tori x ATB. Marmellata and One Roof have the pizza covered, Klay does karak and paratha, and Badou, Fynd and Sadeem are easy café stops. Save room for dessert at Home Bakery, frozen yoghurt at Meli Greek or soft serve at Yuko.

Marsa Boulevard is seasonal – it runs through Dubai's cooler months and closes for the summer – and it's at its busiest on weekend evenings, so go early if you want a waterfront table. We'll keep this guide updated as new spots open through the season.
